1: Injured Ahaziah consults a pagan god. Elijah announces he will die, and fire falls on soldiers sent to arrest the prophet.
2: Elijah parts the Jordan and is carried up in a whirlwind with a chariot of fire. Elisha receives a double share of his spirit and takes up his cloak.
The mission passes from master to disciple.
3: Three kings march against Moab and run out of water. Elisha promises water and victory.
God helps for the sake of the faithful king of Judah.
4: A widow's oil multiplies to pay her debts. A childless woman is given a son, and Elisha raises him from death. Twenty loaves feed a hundred men.
These miracles anticipate those of Jesus.
5: The Syrian general Naaman is told to wash seven times in the Jordan. He is insulted, then obeys and is healed.
Jesus cites Naaman: God's mercy reaches foreigners. Healing comes through humble obedience.
6: An axe head floats. An army surrounds Elisha, and he prays for his servant's eyes to be opened to see the hills full of horses and chariots of fire.
"Those who are with us are more than those who are with them."
7: Samaria is starving. Elisha foretells plenty by the next day. Four lepers find the enemy camp abandoned.
The lepers say, "This is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent."
8: The Shunammite woman gets her land back. Elisha weeps as he foretells that Hazael will become king of Syria and ravage Israel.
A prophet takes no pleasure in announcing judgement.
9: A prophet anoints Jehu king. He kills the kings of Israel and Judah, and Jezebel is thrown from a window.
The judgement Elijah announced on Ahab's house arrives.
10: Jehu wipes out Ahab's family and the worshippers of Baal, but keeps the golden calves.
Zeal against others' sins is not the same as full obedience.
11: Queen Athaliah murders the royal family. One baby, Joash, is hidden in the Temple for six years and then crowned.
David's line survives by a thread.
12: Joash collects money to restore the Temple and pays honest workmen.
He does right while his teacher, the priest Jehoiada, guides him.
13: Israel is oppressed by Syria. The dying Elisha promises victories. Later a dead man revives on touching Elisha's bones.
Catholics see here support for honouring the relics of the saints.
14: Amaziah of Judah is defeated after picking a fight with Israel. Jeroboam II restores Israel's borders.
God shows mercy to Israel despite its kings.
15: Azariah (Uzziah) reigns long in Judah. In Israel five kings rule in quick succession, most murdered, as Assyria closes in.
A kingdom without faithfulness has no stability.
16: Ahaz sacrifices his own son, buys Assyria's help with Temple treasure, and copies a pagan altar.
A king of David's line sinks to pagan practice.
17: Assyria conquers the northern kingdom and deports its people. The writer explains why: they rejected God's covenant and his prophets.
The ten tribes are lost. Foreign settlers become the Samaritans.
18: Hezekiah removes idols and holds fast to the Lord. Sennacherib of Assyria invades, and his officer mocks Jerusalem's faith.
"Do not let Hezekiah deceive you" is the enemy's line in every age.
19: Hezekiah spreads the threatening letter before the Lord and prays. Isaiah promises rescue, and that night the Assyrian army is struck down.
Prayer is Hezekiah's first response to a threat.
20: Told he will die, Hezekiah weeps and prays, and God adds fifteen years. He then shows off his treasures to envoys from Babylon.
Pride after mercy prepares future loss.
21: Manasseh rebuilds the pagan shrines, practises sorcery and sheds innocent blood for fifty-five years.
The worst king of Judah. Exile becomes certain.
22: The book of the law found
During Temple repairs under King Josiah a scroll of the law is found. Josiah tears his clothes on hearing it.
23: Josiah renews the covenant, destroys every idol and shrine, and keeps a great Passover. He dies in battle at Megiddo.
The best of kings cannot undo generations of sin by himself.
24: Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon takes Jerusalem, carries off the king, the craftsmen and the Temple treasures, and installs Zedekiah.
The warnings of the prophets come true.
25: Zedekiah rebels. After a long siege Babylon burns the Temple and the city and takes the people into exile. Years later the captive king Jehoiachin is released.
The story ends in ruin, with one small sign of hope for David's line.
